title: Short HYG — High Yield Credit Spread Widening Under BofA 3-Hike Framework
entry: Short $78–81 (HYG at ~$80.01; enter in stages — 50% immediately, 25% add on any HYG bounce to $81-82 if June 25 PCE is hot and initial credit reaction is delayed, 25% add if HYG breaks below $78 confirming spread widening). Short position accrues HYG's monthly dividend as a carrying cost (~6% annualized, ~0.5% per month) — size accordingly; the thesis must play out within 6-8 weeks to overcome dividend drag. Do NOT short below $77 — at that level most of the spread widening is already discounted.
stop_loss: $84 daily close (~4.8% above $80 short entry) — implies May PCE June 25 undershoots dramatically (core <3.0%), killing the BofA 3-hike thesis and driving a credit rally as rate-cut expectations re-emerge; OR SPX reclaims 7,600+ (risk-on flood that compresses spreads regardless of rate path) — a spread-compression environment at $84+ contradicts the widening thesis across all credit quality tiers
targets: $76 — OAS spread widens from current ~320 bps to ~380 bps as PCE June 25 prints hot (core >3.5%) and September rate hike probability hits 85%; credit markets begin discounting the second and third BofA hikes; leveraged buyouts and high-yield refinancing costs re-price upward; +5.0% short gain from $80 entry

$73 — BofA September hike confirmed (post-FOMC September 2026); credit upgrade cycle reversal as highly-leveraged companies (ICR 2.0x or below) begin showing covenant stress on higher interest expense; HYG OAS widens to 430-450 bps, back toward 2023 levels; +8.75% short gain

$70 — structural widening: BofA third hike (December 2026) confirmed; leveraged loan defaults begin ticking up as maturity walls (2025-2027 vintage leveraged loans at 3-month SOFR + 350bps) reset into a 5.5%+ Fed funds rate; HYG reprices to the low end of its 2022-2023 range; +12.5% short gain
risk_reward: 1:2.5 to third target (excluding ~3% dividend drag over the 8-week holding period)
catalyst: Bank of America's June 22 revised Fed forecast calls for three 25bp hikes in September, October, and December 2026 — citing inflation 'unambiguously worse' and the labor market 'too strong to allow cuts.' Deutsche Bank independently aligned. May PCE (June 25, 8:30 AM ET) is the first definitive inflation data point since the BofA note: consensus is 4.1% YoY headline, 3.3% core. A hot read (core >3.5%) accelerates the 3-hike pricing into credit markets. The current HYG OAS spread of ~320 bps embeds only ~1 additional hike over the next 12 months — three hikes would structurally reprice to ~400 bps. Today's Fed Bank Stress Test results (expected afternoon June 24) may also generate near-term credit market volatility.
thesis:
High yield credit is the last major asset class to reprice the BofA 3-hike framework. Equities have sold off (SPX -95 pts below the 7,460 floor), rates have moved (30Y at 4.94%, 6 bps from the 5% trigger), and the dollar has strengthened (DXY 101.38, above the 100 trigger). But HYG is still trading at $80, implying spread OAS of approximately 320 bps — a level consistent with only one additional hike and a stable credit outlook, not three hikes over five months.

The mechanism of spread widening is mechanical, not macro-judgmental. Three 25bp hikes raise the Fed funds rate to approximately 4.75-5.00% by December 2026. High-yield issuers with floating-rate debt (leveraged loans, CLO tranches) see immediate interest cost increases — an average HY company with $500M in floating debt at SOFR + 350bps sees interest expense rise $37.5M per year per additional hike. For issuers with ICR (interest coverage ratios) below 2.5x, this triggers covenant stress and potentially downgrade risk. The default rate begins to tick up in H1 2027, but spread widening anticipates this 6-12 months in advance. HYG in late 2022 — the last time the market was pricing three 2023 hikes — traded at $68-72. We're not calling for a return to those levels, but a reversion from $80 to $73-76 as the BofA hike path is confirmed is well within the historical precedent.

The HYG short has a known cost: the monthly dividend creates a ~0.5% per month drag on the short position (HYG yields ~6% annualized). Over an 8-week hold, that's approximately 1.0% in dividend payments owed by the short-seller. The first target at $76 (−5.0%) covers the dividend cost with 4.0% net gain; the second and third targets are comfortably above the drag. The position size of 3% accounts for this carry cost while keeping overall credit exposure manageable.

The counter-argument is a PCE undershoot: if May PCE comes in below 3.0% core tomorrow (June 25), the entire 3-hike thesis collapses overnight. Oil at $77.20 Brent (3-month low on Iran normalization) feeds into PCE with a 2-3 month lag, meaning May PCE could genuinely undershoot on energy base effects. This is why the stop at $84 is intentionally tight — the PCE binary on June 25 settles the bull/bear case quickly, and a wrong-way print should be exited immediately.
bull_case: May PCE June 25 prints 4.3% YoY headline, 3.6% core — above consensus. September rate hike probability surges from 68% to 90% on CME FedWatch. HYG falls 3-4% in a single session to $77, approaching first target. 30Y breaks above 5.0% same session, confirming BofA's framework. Over the following 4 weeks, Deutsche Bank and Goldman both align on 3-hike forecast. HYG continues to $73-74 (second target) by end of July as the credit repricing accelerates.
bear_case: May PCE June 25 prints 3.8% YoY, 3.1% core — below the feared 4.1%/3.3% consensus. The market interprets this as the inflation peak, removing one leg of the BofA 3-hike argument. Rate cut odds for December 2026 rise marginally. HYG rallies 2-3% to $82-83. The stop at $84 is not triggered but the short is underwater. Equities rally on the PCE miss (VIX below 17 on the day), compressing credit spreads further on a risk-on rotation into high yield. Exit the position if HYG closes above $84 for two consecutive sessions.
invalidation: $84 daily close; OR May PCE core below 3.0% (disinflation confirmed, 3-hike thesis structurally invalidated); OR BofA or Deutsche Bank reverses the 3-hike call (returns to 1-hike or pause base case); OR Warsh delivers explicitly dovish language before September FOMC that materially reduces hike probability
